body:
PR #1986 (STORY-1351, seat handoff pack): APPROVED — verdict recorded.

Verdict: .aida/review-verdicts/STORY-1351.json + PR-1986.json, sha d941fadc87.

I ran the spec's OWN acceptance test rather than reviewing on reading. Built the branch
binary, init'd a throwaway project against a clean HOME, and read the cold advisor launch
context on both vendors.

RESULT — criterion 1 ("can state from its launch context alone: what it gates, what it
must never do, how it writes a rework brief, what is waiting for it", on Claude AND Codex):
  fresh install, claude  -> all four clauses PASS
  fresh install, codex   -> all four clauses PASS (byte-identical guidance block)
Criterion 2 ("recurring duties appear as due seat jobs within one tick of launch"):
  PASS — mailbox-triage renders under ## Due Jobs on a fresh init.
Criterion 3 ("nothing mechanised in channels 1-2 is delivered as prose"):
  PASS — the PR pins it with a negative assertion, and two-seat-protocol.md defers
  recurring work to `aida schedule due`.

This evidence is what acceptance clause 1 asked to be "recorded on this spec" and had not
been. Please copy it onto STORY-1351 if you want it durable there — I recorded it on the
verdict, which is the reviewer's surface, not the spec's.

A CORRECTION to something I said in an earlier working note, in case it reached you: I
first flagged scope bullet 3 (register the seat cron jobs in the scaffolded [schedule]
defaults) as unimplemented. That was my error — I grepped aida-core/templates/ and the
block is emitted from init_cmd.rs, which I had not read. It IS implemented, and I verified
all three jobs land enabled in a fresh project's .aida/config.toml.

ONE REAL GAP — filed BUG-1464, HIGH, and deliberately NOT blocking:
The new system_prompt never reaches an already-initialized machine.
scaffold_starter_roles skips any existing role file; role_guidance_for falls through to
default_role_guidance when system_prompt is absent; `aida scaffold refresh` does not cover
~/.aida/roles/ at all. Reproduced: on a HOME whose advisor.toml predates the change, the
launch context prints "Purpose:" but no "System prompt:" block, so NOTHING in it names
rework-brief-craft.md — clause (c) fails there. Re-running `aida init` and running
`aida scaffold refresh` both no-op silently.

Why I did not block on it, and where I could be wrong: no regression, and the spec scopes
its acceptance to a cold/fresh seat, which passes on both vendors. But this is STORY-1351's
own thesis — a durable-looking channel that silently carries nothing is the failure mode the
spec exists to kill, and both documented upgrade paths no-op without a warning. If you read
the spec as covering existing machines, this is a RequestChanges and I will revise the
verdict on your word. It is your gate, not mine.

Three lesser findings on the verdict: the PR's own cold-launch test runs against an empty
TempDir so it never exercises the system_prompt path at all; the commented `capture-sweep`
sample job is deleted outright with no basis in the spec; and `product-wave-relaunch` ships
enabled at every=5m telling the product seat to launch a wave (seat- and predicate-gated,
so it cannot self-execute — flagging for visibility, not correction).

MERGE IS BLOCKED ON INFRASTRUCTURE, NOT REVIEW. gh auth on this machine is dead (HTTP 401,
invalid token), so I cannot read CI status or merge either PR. Both #1976 and #1986 are
approved and, in my read, merge-ready once someone runs `gh auth login -h github.com` and
the required check is confirmed green. #1986 is 1 commit behind main but the gap is
docs-only and touches no file the PR touches, so no rebase is needed.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
